topics.label: Introduction and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture as an integration of previously introduced immune cells and molecules.

topics.label: Principles of innate recognition through PAMPs, DAMPs and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate immune recognition distinguishes danger using molecular patterns and appropriately positioned receptors.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how toll-like receptors translate microbial recognition into immune responses suited to the location of the signal.

topics.label: Non-TLR recognition pathways and inflammasome-driven inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how recognition pathways beyond TLRs connect danger sensing to inflammatory activation and disease.

topics.label: Sentinel-driven inflammatory responses and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how activated sentinel cells generate signals that mobilize the inflammatory response.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how infection information travels from tissues to lymph nodes to initiate adaptive immunity.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how excessive inflammatory activation produces life-threatening systemic effects.

topics.label: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammatory activity is shut down through the changing balance of activating and inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what happens when inflamed tissue is restored or remains in a persistent inflammatory state.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The closing ends the lecture and identifies complement as the next lecture's subject.
